source.title: Adaptive Adversarial Cross-Entropy Loss for Sharpness-Aware Minimization

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own SAM/AACE training results on image-classification datasets, but does not test any listed version: its accuracy and loss comparisons do not measure the specific behaviors or properties those versions name.
record.gate_note: The paper’s results compare SAM variants and training methods. Its stated comparisons of gradient magnitudes and perturbation distances are not rows because they do not measure the generalization gap or a listed version’s outcome.
record.test_reason: The study builds on the premise that seeking flat minima improves generalization and reports its SAM/AACE method's performance. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness, correlate it with generalization gaps, compare measure rankings, or test any other listed version. Larger optimizer perturbations are not measurements of tolerance to weight perturbations.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that AACE increases perturbation loss and its gradient near convergence, and that removing gradient normalization increases exploratory perturbations. They report improved classification performance across the tested architectures and datasets; Table 3 qualifies this conclusion because original SAM performs better on PyramidNet/CIFAR-10.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a modified perturbation loss and unnormalized perturbation for SAM; evaluates image-classification accuracy and training/validation loss rather than the claim versions’ tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported results vary with perturbation normalization and rho; PyramidNet’s proposed method is not highest on CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM/AACE exceeds SGD on all eight architecture–dataset combinations and original SAM on seven. PyramidNet on CIFAR-10 reaches 96.52%, below original SAM's 96.95%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM/AACE improves reported image-classification accuracy over SGD and usually over original SAM in these experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: On Wide ResNet/CIFAR-100, the text reports higher training loss but lower validation loss for SAM/AACE than original SAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM/AACE improves validation loss despite worse training loss in this comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: The CIFAR-100 hyperparameter search selects unnormalized AACE perturbations with rho 0.2 at 84.33%; both normalization choices perform poorly at sufficiently large rho.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM/AACE accuracy depends on perturbation normalization and rho.

record.problems: The generalization comparison in Fig. 6 has no numeric values in the supplied text; reported classification tables provide no uncertainty estimates. Hyperparameters and training budgets differ between SGD and SAM in the described comparison.
record.rows_left_out: None; 40 rows recorded. The paper also describes gradient magnitudes and perturbation distances in Fig. 5, but these are not measures of the claim versions or generalization gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy compared with natural-label training under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning; Adam-to-SGD switching and decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size effects within a workload under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout versus no dropout, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and its ranking relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's inconsistent tests/T6 classification with uses_without_test/T4. All listed accuracy values match the supplied tables. SGD receives 400 epochs versus 200 for SAM variants; both SAM variants use SGD as their base optimizer. Different batch sizes across architectures do not constitute a controlled batch-size test. No listed-version result is missing.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting natural labels with fitting random labels or report held-out performance under random labels.
Does not sweep network width past the interpolation threshold or measure test error across widths.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks or test local connectivity.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD under the tuning conditions in the version.
Does not compare batch sizes or test large-batch penalties under fixed epoch budgets.
Does not test magnitude-aware sharpness or compare its ranking of generalization gaps with other measures.
Does not remove memorized examples and measure the effect on test accuracy.
